h: Pair It With the Transport Museum
p: If you want to lean into Coventry's motoring story properly, there's one place you can't miss. The Coventry Transport Museum, in the city centre, is free to visit and houses a huge collection of British-built road transport, from early bicycles to classic cars. It also tells the story of Thrust2 and ThrustSSC, the record-breaking land speed cars, both of which are on display.

It makes a perfect pairing with a race. Do the museum in the morning, soak up the history, then head off in the afternoon to see if any of that engineering genius has rubbed off on your driving. Fair warning: it probably hasn't, but that's half the fun.

While you're in the city centre, the ruins of the old cathedral, bombed in 1940, stand right beside the modern Coventry Cathedral, and the pairing is genuinely moving. The Herbert Art Gallery and Museum is close by too.
The Transport Museum also has a land speed simulator and plenty of interactive bits for children, so it works well as a warm-up for younger racers who are counting down to their session.
Book your karting session ahead at weekends, and leave a bit of breathing room between the museum and your race slot so nobody's rushing to sign in.
